grh_b9f37a8036b530e370bc.title: She Wouldnt Say Yes
paragraphs: Psychiatrist Susan Lane meets irrepressible cartoonist Michael Kent, creator of the mischievous Nixie, and is immediately irritated by his determination to turn every encounter into a romance. Their feud follows them onto a train, through Susanâ€™s treatment of an emotionally troubled young woman, and into a string of schemes in which each tries to prove the other is the one behaving irrationally. Susan insists she is too disciplined and well balanced to fall in love, while Michael keeps forcing her to confront the feelings she is trying to diagnose away. When jealousy and a rival blonde finally push Susan past her professional defenses, she admits that she loves Michael and asks him to marry her. He briefly needles her by walking away, then returns with lilacs, and Susan happily accepts the emotional disorder she had spent the story trying to cure.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Virginia Van Upp, Hans Jacoby, Alexander Hall, Rosalind Russell, and Frank Nelson. Other credited names include Laszlo Gorog as writer, Jimmy Wallington as announcer, and Hy Averback as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].

grh_b92ef20bd5f8daa81609.title: Stairway to Heaven
paragraphs: RAF pilot Peter Carter should die when he jumps from a burning aircraft without a parachute, but a celestial mistake lets him survive long enough to meet and fall in love with American radio operator June. When heaven's messenger returns to correct the error, Peter appeals for the right to keep the life he was accidentally given. On earth, neurologist Frank Reeves diagnoses a brain condition and prepares Peter for surgery; in Peter's other reality, Reeves serves as his advocate before a heavenly court. June proves the depth of their love by offering her own life for Peter, and the court grants the appeal. Peter survives the operation with a new date of death far in the future and the chance to live the life he and June nearly lost.

grh_b907ff8070e3ecd566a7.title: Finger in the Wind
paragraphs: A lifelong pilot's story begins with childhood experiments in flight and carries through service with the Lafayette Escadrille in the First World War, barnstorming and the creation of a small commercial airline. By the next war he has thousands of flying hours but is considered too old for a military commission, so he continues moving vital cargo and passengers. When an important foreign official must make an urgent connection, the pilot refuses to fly through dangerous weather despite pressure to prove his courage. The storm confirms his judgment. Soon afterward he dies at his desk, and friends memorialize the veteran airman on a windswept hill with lines envisioning aviation's future.
